# The v1 archive: mine it for ideas, don't copy it

[`archive/`](archive/) holds the **v1 source tree**, preserved when the v2
rebuild started. Almost every problem v2 faces — camera identity across
re-plugs, backend enumeration, the daemon's flock singleton, homography and
deskew geometry, parallax correction, mDNS discovery — **has already been
solved in there once**. Before designing any of it from scratch, go read how
v1 did it. Hard-won specifics are buried in that code: the identity fallback
chain, the UVC control-ordering quirks, the geometry sign conventions.

**But the code is bad.** It is not a source to copy from — it is a source of
*ideas* and *evidence about the problem*. Take the approach, the edge cases it
learned about, and the constants it earned; leave the structure, the naming,
and the 1,000-line modules. v2 code is written fresh against the interface
skeletons in `src/aprilcam/*/interfaces.py` and the design set in
[`docs/design/`](docs/design/), which are the contract. A wholesale port is a
regression even when it passes tests, because it reimports the design v2 exists
to replace.

The practical rule, from
[`docs/design/development-plan.md`](docs/design/development-plan.md):
**convert, don't rewrite blindly — and don't copy blindly either.** Read v1,
understand what it knew, then write the v2 version.

# Knowledge base

Hard-won operational experience — non-obvious fixes, host/environment setup, and
gotchas you don't want to rediscover — goes in
[`docs/knowledge/`](docs/knowledge/) as a markdown entry (one topic per file,
named for the topic). **Check there before redoing setup work, and add an entry
after any painful debugging session.** This is the home for things like
Raspberry Pi camera bring-up, pending formalization (e.g. Ansible) of those
processes. Example: [`docs/knowledge/raspberry-pi-camera-setup.md`](docs/knowledge/raspberry-pi-camera-setup.md).
